data.narrative:
Cambridge Aerospace, founded by Steven Barrett and Chris Sylvan, is a Series B-stage defense and security company that has raised $300M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 10 firms across the sector—2 public companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private peers—with particular focus on 7 same-stage, same-sector private companies including Dream Security, Harmattan AI, Code Metal, Castelion, and Defense Unicorns.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x multiplier to the $300M total raised as a proxy, implying a valuation of $570M. Peer-median analysis examines the 7 Defense & Security Series B comparables, which span a range of $300M to $3.0B and carry a median valuation of $1.0B, reflecting heterogeneity in company maturity and market position within the cohort.

Synthesizing both methods yields a triangulated range of $484M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median estimate of $785M. The stage-progression method produces a more conservative signal, while peer-median reflects the upper half of the distribution. Key uncertainties include the relative quality of Cambridge Aerospace's technology pipeline versus named peers, customer concentration and contract duration, and timing of Series C market conditions. The $300M–$1.1B band should be treated as indicative pending deeper diligence on unit economics and competitive positioning.
